title: COmprehension Assessment of Simplified medical Texts using generative AI – A Prospective, Double-blind, Randomized Controlled Trial
summary: Medical reports often contain technical terms that are difficult to understand. This study investigates whether simplifying the language using artificial intelligence improves understanding and recall. 200 adult patients are randomly assigned to two equal groups. They read a fictional example medical report written either in technical language or in simplified language. The report does not describe their own examination findings. Immediately after reading, participants answer comprehension questions without access to the report. The same questions are repeated by telephone approximately one week later. Reading time is also measured.
conditions: All patients undergoing MRI or CT

interventions.name:
Control group: reading a standardized synthetic radiological example report written in medical terminology.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Scheduled or completed, clinically indicated CT or MRI examination.
Sufficient German language proficiency to complete the questionnaires.
Written informed consent to participate in the study.
Exclusion criteria:
Cognitive or physical impairments preventing questionnaire completion on paper or tablet.
Language barriers precluding study participation.
Lack of capacity to provide informed consent.
Hospital employees, students or other individuals in a dependent relationship.
